title: Annual mean bleaching of at least 10% gave no clear next-year record link in four Atlantic and Pacific samples, 2003-2018
abstract: We tested whether recorded coral bleaching was linked to a record at the same site in the next year. We used Reef Check records from BCO-DMO 773466, version 2. Predictor years were 2003-2018. Follow-up records extended through 2019. The main model used 5,203 site-years at 1,334 sites in 52 countries. It controlled for site, ocean-year, heat stress, depth, season, and current sample count. The tested bleaching state was an annual mean of at least 10%. Its estimated change in next-year record probability was +3.51 percentage points. The country-cluster 95% interval was -6.97 to +13.99 points. All four planned Atlantic and Pacific period intervals included zero. Intervals with country and year grouping also included zero. A positive early pooled result did not give a clear link in every region and period. The evidence permits meaningful recording changes. It does not show that recording was random. An absent archive record does not prove an absent field visit. Repeat-site selection, few high-bleaching records, unknown visit logs, and uneven archive coverage limit inference. The package provides a derived retention panel, code, source hashes, figures, and numerical checks. It does not measure species loss or air pollution.
